Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model order even in expectation; fixed 99-negative HR@10 therefore supports claims about this benchmark protocol, not full-catalog superiority ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Practical implication: compare SASRec, gBCE-only, recency-pooling-only, support-pooling-only, and combined models using identical users, candidates, splits, seeds, and routing. Report all four category scores and their equal-weight macro-average. Single-component ablations assess isolated changes; combined-versus-single comparisons alone cannot establish interactions.

For paired uncertainty, retain each user’s binary hit for every model. Bootstrap users within each category, preserving model pairing, then recompute macro differences and 95% intervals; report discordant wins/losses. Paired resampling follows retrieval-evaluation practice ([Smucker et al.](https://maroo.cs.umass.edu/getpdf.php?id=744)). One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained checkpoints; they exclude training variability, candidate-resampling variability, and selection optimism. Seed 42 alone cannot establish robustness across training runs.

Repeated architecture, hyperparameter, and checkpoint selection can overfit validation noise ([Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html); [Dwork et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26250683/)). Recommended design: predeclare comparisons, checkpoint frequency, stopping/tie rules, and a capped search allocation per model family; select by the common macro HR@10 and disclose every validation query. Treat selected-winner intervals as descriptive, not independent confirmation. Allocate the shared 43,200 GPU-seconds upfront, counting diagnostics and failed trials; four concurrent slots do not multiply that budget. Report actual compute and tuning opportunities. Freeze the final configuration before host evaluation, without changing the evaluator or consulting test labels.
